userContent.text:
Build an interactive 2D figure from the brief below and the source image.

AUTHORED FIGURE BRIEF:
This figure is a potential energy curve for a pair of hydrogen atoms, drawn on a pale blue field with small green spheres added to show the atomic arrangement at three points along it. A tall gradient arrow at the far left, shaded from cream to orange and labeled Energy, gives the sense of the vertical scale, while the plot's own vertical axis is marked only with a plus sign, a 0, and a minus sign, with a horizontal dashed line drawn across at zero. The horizontal axis is labeled Internuclear distance and ends in a magenta arrow pointing right. One magenta curve drops steeply from the upper left, crosses below zero, reaches a rounded minimum, then rises gradually and levels off toward the zero line at large separation. At the top of the steep branch two green spheres overlap, annotated HH (too close). At the right, two widely separated spheres sit above a magenta dashed line joining the letters H and H, annotated H - - - H (too far). At the bottom of the well two just-touching spheres are labeled H-H, and a short vertical dashed line drops from the minimum to the axis, tagged 74 pm, with a green arrow labeled Bond length pointing to it. The depth and position of the single minimum, read against the two extremes flanking it, mark the separation at which attraction and nuclear repulsion balance and fix the length of a covalent bond.

REQUESTED INTERACTIONS:
- Slider for internuclear distance: learner drags the two hydrogen atoms closer or farther apart, and a point moves along the energy curve from too close through the 74 pm minimum to too far, showing that bond length occurs where attraction and repulsion balance.
- Click for curve regions: learner clicks the repulsive wall, energy well, or far-separated tail, and the corresponding atom sketch is highlighted, making clear why energy rises at very short distance, falls at bonding distance, and approaches zero when atoms separate.

SOURCE FILE: OpenStax Organic Chemistry, chapter 1: Structure and Bonding

There is no blueprint: decide the figure type, elements, labels, controls, and any step sequence yourself.

outputText:
Drag the slider: the point rides the energy curve and the H atoms move together or apart. Energy is lowest at the bond length (74 pm).

// @FIGURE_CODE_BEGIN // Library: svgjs var draw = SVG().addTo(document.getElementById('container')).size('100%', '100%'); var W = 700, H = 520; draw.viewbox(0, 0, W, H); // World mapping: r in pm -> px, energy -> py var RMIN = 0, RMAX = 600, EMIN = -1.15, EMAX = 1.8; var PX0 = 105, PX1 = W - 25, PY0 = 30, PY1 = H - 85; function px(r) { return PX0 + (r - RMIN) / (RMAX - RMIN) * (PX1 - PX0); } function py(E) { return PY1 - (E - EMIN) / (EMAX - EMIN) * (PY1 - PY0); } function morse(r) { var u = 1 - Math.exp(-0.02 * (r - 74)); return u * u - 1; } // Panel draw.rect(PX1 - PX0 + 10, PY1 - PY0 + 6).move(PX0 - 5, PY0 - 3) .fill('#dff1f9').stroke({ color: '#888', width: 1.5 }); // Zero dashed line and axis marks draw.line(PX0 - 5, py(0), PX1 + 5, py(0)).stroke({ color: '#555', width: 1.2, dasharray: '6,5' }); function halo(t) { t.attr({ 'paint-order': 'stroke', stroke: '#dff1f9', 'stroke-width': 4, 'stroke-linejoin': 'round' }); return t; } halo(draw.text('+').move(PX0 - 28, py(0.55) - 10).font({ size: 18, fill: '#333' })); halo(draw.text('0').move(PX0 - 28, py(0) - 10).font({ size: 16, fill: '#333' })); halo(draw.text('−').move(PX0 - 28, py(-0.55) - 10).font({ size: 18, fill: '#333' })); // Energy gradient arrow at far left var grad = draw.gradient('linear', function (add) { add.stop(0, '#e8641c'); add.stop(1, '#fdf3d0'); }).from(0, 0).to(0, 1); var ax = 55, atop = 12, abot = H - 60; draw.polygon((ax - 16) + ',' + (atop + 26) + ' ' + ax + ',' + atop + ' ' + (ax + 16) + ',' + (atop + 26)) .fill(grad).stroke({ color: '#555', width: 1 }); draw.rect(32, abot - atop - 26).move(ax - 16, atop + 26).fill(grad).stroke({ color: '#555', width: 1 }); draw.text('Energy').font({ size: 20, weight: 'bold', fill: '#222' }) .center(ax, (atop + abot) / 2).rotate(-90, ax, (atop + abot) / 2); // X axis label + magenta arrow draw.text('Internuclear distance').font({ size: 18, fill: '#222' }).center((PX0 + PX1) / 2 - 20, H - 30); draw.line(PX1 - 90, H - 34, PX1 - 25, H - 34).stroke({ color: '#d63384', width: 3 }); draw.polygon((PX1 - 32) + ',' + (H - 40) + ' ' + (PX1 - 18) + ',' + (H - 34) + ' ' + (PX1 - 32) + ',' + (H - 28)).fill('#d63384'); // Energy curve (magenta) var pts = []; for (var r = 22; r <= 590; r += 3) { var E = morse(r); if (E > EMAX) continue; pts.push(px(r) + ',' + py(E)); } var curve = draw.polyline(pts.join(' ')).fill('none') .stroke({ color: '#d6248f', width: 4, linecap: 'round' }); // Bond length marker: dashed vertical from minimum down to panel bottom var minX = px(74), minY = py(-1); draw.line(minX, minY, minX, PY1).stroke({ color: '#333', width: 1.2, dasharray: '4,4' }); halo(draw.text('74 pm').font({ size: 15, weight: 'bold', fill: '#2e7d32' }).center(minX, PY1 + 16)); var bl = draw.group(); bl.line(minX + 14, PY1 - 4, minX + 110, PY1 - 4).stroke({ color: '#2e7d32', width: 1.6 }); bl.polygon((minX + 22) + ',' + (PY1 - 9) + ' ' + (minX + 10) + ',' + (PY1 - 4) + ' ' + (minX + 22) + ',' + (PY1 + 1)).fill('#2e7d32'); bl.text('Bond length').font({ size: 15, fill: '#2e7d32' }).move(minX + 112, PY1 - 16); // Labels for the three regimes halo(draw.text('HH (too close)').font({ size: 16, fill: '#1976a2' }).move(px(30), py(1.35))); halo(draw.text('H – – – H (too far)').font({ size: 16, fill: '#d6248f' }).center(px(430), py(0.06))); halo(draw.text('H—H').font({ size: 16, weight: 'bold', fill: '#2e7d32' }).center(px(74), py(-0.42))); // Static atom sketches at the three regimes function atomPair(cx, cy, sep, rad, group) { var g = group || draw.group(); g.circle(rad * 2).fill('#2e8b46').stroke({ color: '#1d5c2f', width: 1.2 }).center(cx - sep / 2, cy); g.circle(rad * 2).fill('#2e8b46').stroke({ color: '#1d5c2f', width: 1.2 }).center(cx + sep / 2, cy); return g; } var sk1 = atomPair(px(38), py(1.62), 6, 14); // overlapping, too close var sk2 = atomPair(px(74), py(-0.62), 26, 14); // touching, bond length var sk3 = atomPair(px(430), py(0.35), 120, 14);// far apart draw.line(px(430) - 38, py(0.12), px(430) + 38, py(0.12)).stroke({ color: '#d6248f', width: 1.2, dasharray: '5,4' }); // Highlight rings for click feedback var rings = [sk1, sk2, sk3].map(function (g) { var bb = g.bbox(); var ring = draw.ellipse(bb.width + 22, bb.height + 22).center(bb.cx, bb.cy) .fill('none').stroke({ color: '#ffb300', width: 3.5 }).opacity(0); return ring; }); // Moving atom pair (slider-driven) at top of panel var mover = draw.group(); var mRing = mover.ellipse(90, 48).fill('none').stroke({ color: '#1976a2', width: 2, dasharray: '4,3' }); var mL = mover.circle(26).fill('#37a05a').stroke({ color: '#1d5c2f', width: 1.5 }); var mR = mover.circle(26).fill('#37a05a').stroke({ color: '#1d5c2f', width: 1.5 }); halo(mover.text('you').font({ size: 11, fill: '#1976a2' })); var mDot = draw.circle(13).fill('#8e1c63').stroke({ color: '#fff', width: 2 }); var captions = [ 'Too close: nuclei repel strongly, energy shoots up', 'Bond length: attraction and repulsion balance — minimum energy', 'Too far: atoms no longer attract, energy → 0' ]; var capTxt = halo(draw.text('').font({ size: 13, fill: '#444' }).move(PX0 + 6, PY1 - 22)); var curR = 74; function update_dist(r) { curR = r; var sep = Math.max(6, Math.min(220, (r / 74) * 30)); var cx = (PX0 + PX1) / 2, cy = PY0 + 26; mL.center(cx - sep / 2, cy); mR.center(cx + sep / 2, cy); mRing.size(sep + 40, 46).center(cx, cy); mover.children()[3].center(cx, cy + 34); var E = morse(r); mDot.center(px(r), py(Math.min(E, EMAX - 0.05))); var region = r < 55 ? 0 : (r <= 210 ? 1 : 2); capTxt.text(captions[region]); rings.forEach(function (ring, i) { ring.opacity(i === region ? 1 : 0); }); } function setRegion(i) { var r = [30, 74, 480][i]; document.getElementById('distInput').value = r; document.getElementById('distVal').value = r; update_dist(r); } // Clickable regions: repulsive wall, well, tail var regions = [ { x0: 20, x1: 55, ring: 0, title: 'Repulsive wall (too close)', body: 'When the two nuclei are pushed closer than the bond length, nucleus–nucleus repulsion and electron-cloud overlap dominate, so the potential energy rises very steeply. This is why the HH pair here is "too close".' }, { x0: 55, x1: 210, ring: 1, title: 'The energy well (bond forms)', body: 'Near 74 pm the attraction between each nucleus and the shared electron pair exactly balances nuclear repulsion. The energy reaches its minimum — the most stable arrangement — and this separation is the covalent bond length of H₂.' }, { x0: 210, x1: 590, ring: 2, title: 'Far-separated tail (too far)', body: 'As the atoms move apart, the shared-electron attraction weakens and the energy climbs back toward zero, the energy of two isolated H atoms. Beyond a few bond lengths the atoms no longer feel each other — no bond.' } ]; regions.forEach(function (rg) { draw.rect(px(rg.x1) - px(rg.x0), PY1 - PY0).move(px(rg.x0), PY0) .fill('#fff').opacity(0).css('cursor', 'pointer') .on('mousemove', function (e) { showTooltip(rg.title + ' — click to learn more', e); }) .on('mouseleave', function () { hideTooltip(); }) .on('click', function () { setRegion(rg.ring); showPopup(rg.title, rg.body); }); }); curve.css('cursor', 'pointer') .on('mousemove', function (e) { showTooltip('Click a region of the curve', e); }) .on('mouseleave', function () { hideTooltip(); }); update_dist(74); window.__markRendered(); // @FIGURE_CODE_END
